area: Synthesized katana/impact SFX recipes (WebAudio-only, SESSION 25 / Stage 6)

items.title: Sword whoosh = two filtered-noise layers with swept bandpass; heavy-vs-light falls out of envelope length + center frequency
items.claim: Canonical recipe: white noise via AudioBuffer (data[i]=Math.random()*2-1) -> BiquadFilterNode type 'bandpass' whose frequency is ramped (e.g. linearRampToValueAtTime) across the swing, inside a gain envelope (fast attack, ~0.15-0.4s decay). Practitioner refinement (Tsugi, GameSynth medieval-weapons postmortem): use TWO noise layers — one low-emphasized (body of the swing) and one airy high band — and make the HEAVIER weapon's whoosh simply a LONGER envelope + lower band center. MDN's own noise+bandpass demo uses 400-1200 Hz band range (1000 Hz default) as a sane sweep window. Parameterize per-layer: bandStartHz, bandEndHz, filterQ, attackS, decayS, gainPeak — six nameable constants per layer, all INFERRED.

sources.title: MDN — Web Audio API Advanced techniques (noise buffer + bandpass + envelopes)
Tsugi blog — Medieval Weapons Sound Design part 1 (sword whoosh = two noise sources, different filters/envelope durations)
Sonoport — Synthesising Sounds with Web Audio API (noise/filter/envelope node graphs with numbers)

items.adjudication_reason: docs/MASTER_SPEC.md Stage 6 items 1+4 require draw (slashStarted) and whiff (missed) SFX with a heavy-vs-light tone difference — this recipe delivers both from one parameter set. Constants must land in a new src/config/sfx.ts following the src/config/fx.ts `as const` + INFERRED-label idiom (src/config/CLAUDE.md), then be ear-tuned against reference/videos in SESSION 25.
items.implementation_note: Suggested shape: export const WHOOSH_SFX = { layers: [{bandStartHz, bandEndHz, q, attackS, decayS, gain}], heavy: {decayMul, bandHzMul} } as const. Keep the SFX player in src/game (render-only), triggered by SimEvents drained per MASTER_SPEC's GameScene contract (Sim emits SimEvent[] for FX/SFX). Pre-generate one shared noise AudioBuffer of ~1-2s and reuse it for every play.

items.title: Metal clang (armor/parry) = inharmonic square-bank OR fast-decay inharmonic FM; both are plain-node, fully parameterizable
items.claim: Two proven plain-node routes to 'metal'. (a) Additive/inharmonic bank (classic 808-cymbal topology, full numbers in the Sonoport source): 6 square oscillators at fundamental 40 Hz x ratios [2, 3, 4.16, 5.43, 6.79, 8.21] -> bandpass ~10 kHz -> highpass ~7 kHz -> exponential gain decay ~0.05s (lengthen to ~0.2-0.5s and drop the highpass cutoff for a ringing clang rather than a tick). (b) FM: carrier >1000 Hz, modulator at a NON-INTEGER ratio (e.g. 3.57, 7.12 — integer ratios go bell-harmonic, non-integer goes clangorous), modulation depth starting high (~1000+), very fast attack + quick decay; WAC-2016 tutorial states FM beats subtractive for metallic hits. Nameable constants: fundamentalHz, partialRatios[], bpHz, hpHz, decayS (route a); carrierHz, modRatio, modDepthPeak, modDepthDecayS, ampDecayS (route b).

sources.title: Sonoport — Synthesising Sounds with Web Audio API (hi-hat: 6 squares at inharmonic ratios + BP/HP + envelope, all values)
WAC 2016 percussion-synthesis tutorial (irritant) — FM hi-hat/cymbal: carrier >1 kHz, non-integer mod ratio, depth ~1000+

items.adjudication_reason: Directly serves docs/MASTER_SPEC.md Stage 6 item 1 'armor (blocked)' SFX and gate checkbox 28 ('Four-way slash SFX fire on measured frame'). Seed values are generic-cymbal, not OG — every number goes into src/config/sfx.ts as INFERRED per src/config/CLAUDE.md and is re-tuned by ear against the OG parry sound in reference/videos.
items.implementation_note: Prefer route (a) additive bank as the primary: it is deterministic per parameter set, trivially jitterable (scale all partial frequencies by one pitch factor), and every constant is a plain number. Keep route (b) FM as the fallback if the bank sounds too 'hi-hat' next to the OG clang.

items.title: Flesh/body thud = 3-layer percussion recipe: pitch-dropping low tone + short mid attack tone + lowpassed noise burst
items.claim: The consensus layered recipe (kick/snare topology repurposed): LAYER 1 body — sine/triangle starting ~100-120 Hz ramping down toward near-zero (Sonoport kick: 120 Hz -> 0.001 Hz and gain 1 -> 0.001 exponential over 0.5s; shorten to ~0.15-0.3s for a hit rather than a drum); LAYER 2 attack — midrange tone with a much faster, more pronounced decay; LAYER 3 texture — white-noise burst through a lowpass with LOW Q at moderately-high cutoff, decaying over the whole sound (WAC-2016 snare noise layer). Sound-design guidance for punches confirms the same decomposition: sharp slap attack + meaty thud body + subtle texture. Nameable constants: bodyStartHz, bodyEndHz, bodyDecayS, attackHz, attackDecayS, noiseLpHz, noiseLpQ, noiseDecayS, per-layer gains.

sources.title: Sonoport — Synthesising Sounds with Web Audio API (kick: 120 Hz->0.001 pitch drop + exponential gain ramp, 0.5s; snare noise layer)
WAC 2016 percussion-synthesis tutorial — snare = body tone + attack tone + lowpassed low-Q noise, each with own envelope
Pixflow — Punch & impact sound effects for fight scenes (attack/body/texture layer decomposition)

items.adjudication_reason: Serves docs/MASTER_SPEC.md Stage 6 item 1 'flesh (hitLanded)'. All seed numbers are drum-generic; per src/config/CLAUDE.md they enter src/config/sfx.ts labeled INFERRED and get ear-tuned in SESSION 25 against the OG hit sound audible in reference/videos.
items.implementation_note: exponentialRampToValueAtTime cannot ramp to 0 — use 0.001 as the floor exactly as the Sonoport recipes do, then stop() the source. One shared function makeThud(cfg) covers flesh hit AND (with longer bodyDecayS) any future heavy-landing sound.

items.title: Anti-repetition: per-play pitch jitter around +-20% plus slight gain jitter, applied at the render-layer SFX player
items.claim: Established practice: randomize per-play pitch within roughly 80-120% (the +-20% figure is the repeatedly cited baseline for frequently-fired sounds like footsteps), add small volume variation, and never retrigger an identical instance back-to-back — immediate exact repetition is what players notice most. For synthesized SFX this is trivial: multiply every layer's frequency-type constant by one random pitchFactor and the master gain by one gainFactor per play. Nameable constants: pitchJitterPct (seed 0.10-0.20 — a synthesized clang tolerates less than a footstep sample), gainJitterPct (seed ~0.10).

sources.title: Game Audio Learning Portal — How audio is manipulated in games (randomized pitch/volume bounds per playback)
A Sound Effect — How to maintain immersion + reduce repetition in game audio (practitioner roundup)
Bugnet blog — How to fix sound effects sounding too repetitive (+-20% pitch, >=6 variations, no immediate repeats)

items.adjudication_reason: Compatible as-is with the architecture: SFX lives in src/game (render-only per src/game/CLAUDE.md), driven by drained SimEvents from src/core/Sim.ts, so jitter randomness never touches the deterministic Sim — the no-Math.random invariant (tests/config-purity.test.ts) applies to src/core only. Jitter ranges become two INFERRED constants in src/config/sfx.ts.
items.implementation_note: One caveat vs the generic advice: the OG game may have had ZERO variation (Flash-era games often fired one fixed sound per event). If the videos show identical repeated hits, per the prime directive set pitchJitterPct to 0 and keep the mechanism dormant — the constant existing costs nothing.

items.title: Before seeding any INFERRED SFX constant: extract and spectrogram the OG audio from the two reference videos
items.claim: The professional workflow the Tsugi postmortem describes for its sword impact — 'extract resonant modes from analyzed samples', then synthesize to match — applies directly here, and this repo is uniquely positioned: the OG SFX are IN the ground-truth videos. ffmpeg-extract the audio track, cut the whoosh/clang/flesh/draw one-shots at the already-measured attack frames, and read center frequency, band width, duration, and pitch-drop shape off a spectrogram. That converts SESSION 25's 'tune by ear' into 'tune by ear from measured seeds', and lets several sfx.ts constants be tagged CONTRACT (measured) instead of INFERRED.

sources.title: Tsugi blog — Medieval Weapons Sound Design part 1 (impact model built from resonant modes extracted from analyzed samples)

items.adjudication_reason: CLAUDE.md invariant: 'THE TWO GAMEPLAY VIDEOS ARE THE PRIMARY 1:1 REFERENCE... Copy what is in them, directly' — and docs/research/fidelity/COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md establishes the measured-row pattern (its §S24 block) that audio rows should join. Generic recipe constants adopted without checking the videos' actual SFX would be exactly the second-hand-grading failure the invariant warns about.
items.implementation_note: ffmpeg -i <video> -vn -acodec pcm_s16le og-audio.wav, then cut one-shots at the ledger's known hit frames and view with sox spectrogram or ffmpeg showspectrumpic. Add the measured rows (centerHz, durationMs, pitch-drop) to COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md before writing src/config/sfx.ts.
items.stage: SESSION 25, first task before any synthesis code

items.title: Karplus-Strong / AudioWorklet string synthesis for the clang: skip it
items.claim: Practitioner Web Audio KS implementations either use the deprecated ScriptProcessorNode or require AudioWorklet processors (with Wasm recommended for performance and SharedArrayBuffer messaging to avoid GC glitches, per the karplus-stress-tester benchmark and the mrahtz implementation). That is an entire extra build surface (worklet bundling under Vite, cross-origin isolation for SAB) to produce a plucked-string timbre the spec never asks for — the inharmonic-bank/FM clang (item 2) reaches 'metal' with plain OscillatorNode/BiquadFilterNode graphs. UI ticks likewise need nothing beyond a single short oscillator blip with a fast exponential decay (the Sonoport hi-hat topology shortened), and are not in the Stage 6 SFX list at all — only add one if the OG videos' menu audio demonstrably has one.

sources.title: Jack Schaedler — Karplus-Strong stress tester (AudioWorklet per-node overhead; Wasm+SAB needed for clean performance)
mrahtz/javascript-karplus-strong — JS/Web Audio KS guitar synthesis (asm.js-era implementation burden)
WAC 2016 percussion-synthesis tutorial — 'FM does a better job of synthesizing metallic sounds than subtractive'

items.adjudication_reason: Churn: docs/MASTER_SPEC.md Stage 6 names exactly four SFX + two music beds + two stings, and src/config/CLAUDE.md's landmine forbids inventing constants/systems that 'feel missing'. Item 2's plain-node recipes cover the only metallic requirement ('armor (blocked)'); an AudioWorklet KS pipeline serves no gate checkbox.

dead_ends: The jackschaedler karplus-stress-tester page did NOT document the commonly-repeated '128-sample render-quantum minimum for DelayNode feedback loops' claim, so that specific pitch-ceiling figure is omitted as ungrounded (the REJECT stands on implementation-burden evidence alone). The FXive procedural-synthesis paper surfaced only as a ResearchGate PDF stub and was not fetched. No practitioner source publishes a verbatim 'sword parry clang in Web Audio' recipe — the clang item is synthesized from the adjacent cymbal/FM-metal recipes and flagged for by-ear/spectrogram tuning. COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS.md contains zero audio rows (the only grep hit, 'SOUND360TM', is a player name), confirming OG SFX are entirely unmeasured — hence the MEASURE_FIRST item.
